ibs.title: Irritable bowel syndrome
ibs.lead: IBS combines recurrent abdominal pain with changes in stool frequency or consistency.
paragraphs: IBS combines recurrent abdominal pain with changes in stool frequency or consistency. Constipation, diarrhoea and mixed patterns describe different experiences of the disorder.
Fermentation, intestinal transit, visceral sensitivity and gut–brain signalling interact. Research examines how microbial metabolites affect these processes and how dietary changes alter symptoms.
Assessment looks at the symptom pattern and features suggesting another condition. Treatment can combine dietary adjustments, soluble fibre, medicines and gut-directed psychological therapies.
ibs.author: Gut Atlas seed

constipation.title: Chronic constipation
constipation.lead: Constipation involves difficult, infrequent or incomplete bowel movements.
paragraphs: Constipation involves difficult, infrequent or incomplete bowel movements. Stool hardness, straining and a sense of blockage can matter as much as how often someone goes.
Time spent in the colon changes water absorption and microbial metabolism. Methane-producing archaea are studied in relation to slower transit, alongside pelvic-floor and medication effects.
Care starts with the pattern, medicines and examination. Fibre, fluid, activity, laxatives or pelvic-floor treatment address different causes; bleeding or persistent new symptoms deserve assessment.
constipation.author: Gut Atlas seed

microscopic-colitis.title: Microscopic colitis
microscopic-colitis.lead: Microscopic colitis causes chronic watery diarrhoea, often without visible bleeding.
paragraphs: Microscopic colitis causes chronic watery diarrhoea, often without visible bleeding. The colon can look normal during endoscopy; tissue samples reveal the inflammation.
Researchers study the intestinal barrier, bile acids, medication exposure and microbial communities in the inflamed colon. These are distinct targets from the visible lesions of ulcerative colitis.
Diagnosis requires colonic biopsies. Care includes reviewing medicines and triggers, managing fluid loss and using treatments such as budesonide when indicated.
microscopic-colitis.author: Gut Atlas seed

crohns.title: Crohn’s disease
crohns.lead: Crohn’s disease produces patchy inflammation anywhere along the digestive tract.
paragraphs: Crohn’s disease produces patchy inflammation anywhere along the digestive tract. It can affect the full bowel wall and cause pain, diarrhoea, weight loss, narrowing or fistulas.

The immune system interacts abnormally with intestinal contents and microbes. Human studies identify changes in community function; experiments investigate barrier damage, microbial products and inflammatory responses.
Endoscopy, imaging, laboratory tests and biopsies help establish the diagnosis. Anti-inflammatory or immune-targeted medicines, nutritional support and sometimes surgery control complications.
crohns.author: Gut Atlas seed

ulcerative-colitis.title: Ulcerative colitis
ulcerative-colitis.lead: Ulcerative colitis inflames the colon’s inner lining, usually beginning in the rectum.
paragraphs: Ulcerative colitis inflames the colon’s inner lining, usually beginning in the rectum. Bloody diarrhoea, urgency and abdominal pain can alternate with periods of remission.
Microbial metabolites, mucus and mucosal immune responses are active research areas. Donor-microbiota trials investigate whether changing a community can help induce remission.
Treatment depends on extent and severity and can include mesalamine, immune-targeted therapy or surgery. Follow-up also addresses nutrition and colorectal-cancer surveillance.
ulcerative-colitis.author: Gut Atlas seed

coeliac.title: Coeliac disease
coeliac.lead: Coeliac disease is an immune response to gluten that damages the small-intestinal lining.
paragraphs: Coeliac disease is an immune response to gluten that damages the small-intestinal lining. It can cause diarrhoea, bloating, iron deficiency or symptoms beyond digestion.
Damaged villi change nutrient absorption and the substrates available to microbes. Studies examine microbial gluten processing and the community’s interaction with intestinal immunity.
Blood tests and sometimes intestinal biopsy support diagnosis while gluten is still being eaten. Treatment is a lifelong gluten-free diet with attention to nutritional recovery.
coeliac.author: Gut Atlas seed

gerd.title: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease
gerd.lead: GERD occurs when reflux repeatedly causes troublesome symptoms or tissue injury.
paragraphs: GERD occurs when reflux repeatedly causes troublesome symptoms or tissue injury. Heartburn and regurgitation are common; some people develop inflammation or narrowing of the oesophagus.

The oesophagus and stomach contain distinct microbial habitats. Research examines reflux-associated changes in these communities and the effects of acid-suppressing medicines on downstream gut ecology.
Care can include adjusting meal timing, addressing individual triggers and acid suppression. Swallowing difficulty, bleeding or unexplained weight loss call for assessment.
gerd.author: Gut Atlas seed

functional-dyspepsia.title: Functional dyspepsia
functional-dyspepsia.lead: Functional dyspepsia causes persistent upper-abdominal discomfort, early fullness or burning without a structural explanation for the symptoms.
paragraphs: Functional dyspepsia causes persistent upper-abdominal discomfort, early fullness or burning without a structural explanation for the symptoms. It can overlap with IBS.
Research follows stomach accommodation, gastric emptying, duodenal immune activity and microbial exposure. H. pylori infection is a separate, testable contributor to dyspeptic symptoms.
Evaluation considers H. pylori, medicines and warning signs. Treatment is tailored to pain, fullness and the person’s other findings.
functional-dyspepsia.author: Gut Atlas seed

peptic-ulcer.title: Peptic ulcer disease
peptic-ulcer.lead: Peptic ulcers are breaks in the lining of the stomach or duodenum.
paragraphs: Peptic ulcers are breaks in the lining of the stomach or duodenum. H. pylori infection and anti-inflammatory pain medicines are major causes; ulcers can bleed or perforate.
H. pylori is a direct microbial cause, working within the stomach’s mucus and acid environment. Ulcers caused by medicines follow another route to injury.
Testing and treatment address H. pylori, acid exposure and ulcer-provoking medicines. Vomiting blood, black stools or sudden severe abdominal pain need urgent care.
peptic-ulcer.author: Gut Atlas seed

gastritis.title: Gastritis
gastritis.lead: Gastritis is inflammation of the stomach lining.
paragraphs: Gastritis is inflammation of the stomach lining. H. pylori, autoimmune disease and other exposures can produce different forms, with or without obvious symptoms.
The gastric environment selects acid-tolerant organisms. H. pylori-driven inflammation and autoimmune loss of acid-producing cells change that environment in different ways.
Investigation may include H. pylori testing, blood tests or endoscopy. Treatment follows the cause and can also address iron or vitamin B12 deficiency.
gastritis.author: Gut Atlas seed

lactose-intolerance.title: Lactose intolerance
lactose-intolerance.lead: Lactose intolerance causes gas, bloating or diarrhoea when too little lactase is available to digest milk sugar.
paragraphs: Lactose intolerance causes gas, bloating or diarrhoea when too little lactase is available to digest milk sugar. The amount tolerated varies with the food and portion.
Undigested lactose reaches microbes that ferment it into acids and gases. Live yoghurt cultures can supply enzymes that assist lactose digestion during a meal.
People often manage symptoms by adjusting portions, choosing low-lactose foods or using lactase. New symptoms after an infection or bowel disease can reflect temporary loss of lactase.
lactose-intolerance.author: Gut Atlas seed

fructose-malabsorption.title: Fructose malabsorption
fructose-malabsorption.lead: Poor absorption of a large fructose load can leave sugar in the intestine, producing bloating, gas and loose stools.
paragraphs: Poor absorption of a large fructose load can leave sugar in the intestine, producing bloating, gas and loose stools. This differs from hereditary fructose intolerance.
Unabsorbed fructose draws water and becomes a fermentation substrate. Its effects depend on dose, accompanying sugars, transit and the microbial community.
A dietary history helps identify the pattern. A dietitian can guide targeted changes and reintroduction without unnecessarily excluding broad groups of fruit or vegetables.
fructose-malabsorption.author: Gut Atlas seed

sibo.title: Small-intestinal bacterial overgrowth
sibo.lead: SIBO describes excessive or altered bacterial growth in the small intestine.
paragraphs: SIBO describes excessive or altered bacterial growth in the small intestine. It can accompany impaired motility, altered anatomy or other disease and produce bloating, diarrhoea or malabsorption.
Location matters: organisms and fermentation processes that belong further downstream encounter nutrients earlier. Breath gases provide an indirect measurement of this activity.
Assessment considers the underlying cause and the limitations of breath testing. Treatment may involve antibiotics, correcting contributing conditions and nutritional support.
sibo.author: Gut Atlas seed

gallstones.title: Gallstones
gallstones.lead: Gallstones form from components of bile.
paragraphs: Gallstones form from components of bile. Many cause no symptoms; a stone blocking a duct can cause severe pain, infection or pancreatitis.
The liver–bile–gut circuit connects digestion with microbial bile-acid transformations. Studies examine how these transformations and metabolic conditions relate to stone formation.
Symptomatic stones often require gallbladder removal or procedures to clear a duct. Fever, jaundice or persistent severe upper-abdominal pain require prompt assessment.
gallstones.author: Gut Atlas seed

acute-pancreatitis.title: Acute pancreatitis
acute-pancreatitis.lead: Acute pancreatitis is sudden inflammation of the pancreas.
paragraphs: Acute pancreatitis is sudden inflammation of the pancreas. Gallstones and alcohol are common causes, and severe disease can affect circulation and other organs.
Severe inflammation can disturb gut motility and barrier function. Research studies microbial translocation and nutrition during recovery, alongside the pancreatic injury itself.
Hospital care addresses fluids, pain, nutrition and the cause. Severe persistent upper-abdominal pain with vomiting needs urgent medical attention.
acute-pancreatitis.author: Gut Atlas seed

chronic-pancreatitis.title: Chronic pancreatitis
chronic-pancreatitis.lead: Repeated or persistent pancreatic injury can cause scarring, chronic pain and loss of digestive enzyme production.
paragraphs: Repeated or persistent pancreatic injury can cause scarring, chronic pain and loss of digestive enzyme production. Diabetes and poor nutrient absorption can follow.
Changes in enzyme delivery alter what is digested before reaching intestinal microbes. Malabsorption and microbial overgrowth can compound nutritional problems.
Care addresses the cause, pain, nutrition and diabetes. Pancreatic enzyme replacement supports digestion when enzyme production is insufficient.
chronic-pancreatitis.author: Gut Atlas seed

fatty-liver.title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
fatty-liver.lead: MASLD involves excess liver fat in a metabolic setting such as insulin resistance or obesity.
paragraphs: MASLD involves excess liver fat in a metabolic setting such as insulin resistance or obesity. Some people develop inflammation, fibrosis and eventually cirrhosis.
Blood from the intestine flows directly to the liver. Microbial products, bile acids and intestinal permeability are investigated along this gut–liver route.
Assessment estimates liver injury and fibrosis as well as metabolic risk. Nutrition, sustained activity, weight management and appropriate medical treatment support liver health.
fatty-liver.author: Gut Atlas seed

diverticular-disease.title: Diverticular disease
diverticular-disease.lead: Diverticula are pouches in the colon wall.
paragraphs: Diverticula are pouches in the colon wall. They are common with age; some people develop associated pain, bleeding or inflammation.
Stool consistency, transit and diet shape the environment around the pouches. Microbial and immune changes are investigated in symptomatic disease.
Care depends on whether the issue is symptoms, bleeding or acute inflammation. Gradual dietary fibre changes can support bowel function after assessment.
diverticular-disease.author: Gut Atlas seed

diverticulitis.title: Diverticulitis
diverticulitis.lead: Diverticulitis occurs when one or more colonic pouches become inflamed.
paragraphs: Diverticulitis occurs when one or more colonic pouches become inflamed. It can cause localised pain and fever, with abscesses or perforation in complicated cases.
The local bowel wall and its microbes are involved in inflammation. This differs from simply having diverticula or a particular stool-community profile.
Clinical assessment and sometimes imaging establish severity. Treatment ranges from supportive care to antibiotics, drainage or surgery for specific complications.
diverticulitis.author: Gut Atlas seed

appendicitis.title: Appendicitis
appendicitis.lead: Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix.
paragraphs: Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix. Pain often progresses and localises to the lower-right abdomen, sometimes with nausea or fever.
The appendix contains lymphoid tissue and a dense microbial community. Research examines obstruction, local bacterial growth and immune responses during inflammation.
Suspected appendicitis needs urgent assessment. Surgery and, in selected cases, antibiotics are treatment options chosen according to severity and complications.
appendicitis.author: Gut Atlas seed

haemorrhoids.title: Haemorrhoids
haemorrhoids.lead: Haemorrhoids are enlarged vascular cushions around the anus and lower rectum.
paragraphs: Haemorrhoids are enlarged vascular cushions around the anus and lower rectum. They can cause bleeding, itching, discomfort or prolapse.
The practical gut connection is stool consistency and straining. Supporting comfortable bowel movements reduces repeated mechanical stress.
Care often starts with fibre, fluid and bowel habits, with procedures for persistent problems. Rectal bleeding should be assessed rather than automatically attributed to haemorrhoids.
haemorrhoids.author: Gut Atlas seed

anal-fissure.title: Anal fissure
anal-fissure.lead: An anal fissure is a tear in the anal lining, often causing sharp pain during bowel movements and a small amount of bright blood..
paragraphs: An anal fissure is a tear in the anal lining, often causing sharp pain during bowel movements and a small amount of bright blood.
Hard stool, diarrhoea and sphincter tension can perpetuate injury. The relevant ecological route is through transit and stool properties rather than a named pathogenic organism.
Softening stool and treating pain support healing. Persistent fissures may need prescribed topical treatment or a procedure after examination.
anal-fissure.author: Gut Atlas seed

gastroparesis.title: Gastroparesis
gastroparesis.lead: Gastroparesis slows stomach emptying without a physical blockage.
paragraphs: Gastroparesis slows stomach emptying without a physical blockage. Early fullness, nausea, vomiting and difficulty maintaining nutrition can result.
Delayed delivery of food changes conditions along the digestive tract. Gastric motility, diabetes-related nerve changes and downstream bacterial overgrowth are related research areas.
Diagnosis usually involves an emptying study after excluding obstruction. Meals, medicines, glucose management and nutritional support are adjusted to the severity.
gastroparesis.author: Gut Atlas seed

pancreatic-insufficiency.title: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency
pancreatic-insufficiency.lead: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency means too few pancreatic enzymes reach the intestine.
paragraphs: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency means too few pancreatic enzymes reach the intestine. Fatty stools, weight loss and deficiencies of fat-soluble vitamins can result.
Poorly digested nutrients change microbial substrate supply. The primary problem is enzyme delivery, which can coexist with changes in the intestinal community.
Evaluation can include stool elastase and assessment of the underlying pancreatic disease. Enzyme replacement with meals and nutritional monitoring are central to care.
pancreatic-insufficiency.author: Gut Atlas seed

colorectal-cancer.title: Colorectal cancer
colorectal-cancer.lead: Colorectal cancer begins in the colon or rectum, often developing through precancerous growths.
paragraphs: Colorectal cancer begins in the colon or rectum, often developing through precancerous growths. Screening can identify lesions before symptoms appear.
Studies investigate microbial toxins, inflammation and organisms such as Fusobacterium nucleatum in tumours. Diet, metabolites and the local tissue environment are part of this research.
Screening, colonoscopy and tissue diagnosis guide care. Treatment depends on location, stage and tumour biology and can include surgery and systemic therapies.
colorectal-cancer.author: Gut Atlas seed

stomach-cancer.title: Stomach cancer
stomach-cancer.lead: Stomach cancer can develop after long-standing changes in the gastric lining.
paragraphs: Stomach cancer can develop after long-standing changes in the gastric lining. H. pylori is an important cause of non-cardia gastric cancer.
This is a major example of a microbial infection contributing to cancer risk. Long-term trials follow how eradicating H. pylori changes that risk.
Endoscopy and biopsy establish the diagnosis. Treatment depends on stage and tumour features; treating H. pylori is also important in prevention and relevant follow-up.
stomach-cancer.author: Gut Atlas seed

salmonellosis.title: Salmonellosis
salmonellosis.lead: Non-typhoidal Salmonella commonly causes diarrhoea, fever and abdominal cramps after contaminated food or contact.
paragraphs: Non-typhoidal Salmonella commonly causes diarrhoea, fever and abdominal cramps after contaminated food or contact. Severe infection can enter the bloodstream.
Salmonella interacts with intestinal microbes and uses the inflamed gut environment to compete. Colonisation resistance and host inflammation are studied together.
Replacing lost fluids is central. Antibiotics are reserved for particular patients or severe infection; dehydration, blood in stool or persistent fever require assessment.
salmonellosis.author: Gut Atlas seed

campylobacteriosis.title: Campylobacter infection
campylobacteriosis.lead: Campylobacter infection is a common foodborne cause of diarrhoea and abdominal pain.
paragraphs: Campylobacter infection is a common foodborne cause of diarrhoea and abdominal pain. Undercooked poultry, contaminated water and animal contact are common routes.
The bacterium infects the intestinal lining and can trigger inflammation. Some people develop post-infectious IBS or other complications after the acute infection resolves.
Most cases improve with supportive care. Severe illness or higher-risk patients may need antibiotics selected with local resistance in mind.
campylobacteriosis.author: Gut Atlas seed

shigellosis.title: Shigellosis
shigellosis.lead: Shigella spreads readily by the faecal–oral route and can cause fever, cramps and bloody diarrhoea.
paragraphs: Shigella spreads readily by the faecal–oral route and can cause fever, cramps and bloody diarrhoea. Small inocula can cause infection.
The organism invades the colonic lining and provokes inflammation. Microbial competition, mucosal immunity and antimicrobial resistance shape infection research.
Fluid replacement and infection control matter. Testing can help guide antibiotic treatment because resistance patterns vary and increasingly limit options.
shigellosis.author: Gut Atlas seed

stec.title: Shiga toxin-producing E. coli infection
stec.lead: STEC infection can cause severe abdominal cramps and bloody diarrhoea.
paragraphs: STEC infection can cause severe abdominal cramps and bloody diarrhoea. Shiga toxin can damage blood vessels and cause haemolytic uraemic syndrome.
This is a strain-specific pathogenic function within a much larger E. coli group. Toxin production and host susceptibility explain why species names alone are insufficient.
Suspected infection needs clinical assessment and stool testing. Antibiotics and anti-diarrhoeal medicines can be inappropriate in STEC; hydration and monitoring for complications are important.
stec.author: Gut Atlas seed

rotavirus.title: Rotavirus gastroenteritis
rotavirus.lead: Rotavirus causes vomiting and diarrhoea, particularly in young children, and can produce dangerous dehydration.
paragraphs: Rotavirus causes vomiting and diarrhoea, particularly in young children, and can produce dangerous dehydration. Vaccination has greatly reduced severe disease.
The virus infects intestinal cells. Research examines how intestinal communities and immune development influence infection and oral-vaccine responses.
Oral rehydration is central, with urgent care for significant dehydration. Vaccination is an effective preventive measure according to the local childhood schedule.
rotavirus.author: Gut Atlas seed

cryptosporidiosis.title: Cryptosporidiosis
cryptosporidiosis.lead: Cryptosporidium is a protozoal parasite that causes watery diarrhoea, often after contaminated water or contact.
paragraphs: Cryptosporidium is a protozoal parasite that causes watery diarrhoea, often after contaminated water or contact. Disease can be persistent in people with weakened immunity.
The parasite develops at the intestinal cell surface. Nutritional status, immunity and interactions with the surrounding microbial community affect the research questions.
Treatment addresses dehydration, the parasite when indicated and immune status. Persistent or severe diarrhoea warrants assessment; water and hygiene measures reduce transmission.
cryptosporidiosis.author: Gut Atlas seed

amoebiasis.title: Amoebiasis
amoebiasis.lead: Entamoeba histolytica can cause colitis and bloody diarrhoea and sometimes spreads to the liver.
paragraphs: Entamoeba histolytica can cause colitis and bloody diarrhoea and sometimes spreads to the liver. Other Entamoeba species have different clinical significance.
The parasite interacts with mucus, bacteria and host tissue. Distinguishing pathogenic E. histolytica from other species matters more than finding the genus name alone.
Diagnosis uses appropriate stool or other tests. Treatment targets invasive infection and organisms remaining in the bowel, with regimens chosen by a clinician.
amoebiasis.author: Gut Atlas seed

ascariasis.title: Ascariasis
ascariasis.lead: Ascaris roundworms are acquired by swallowing eggs from contaminated soil or food.
paragraphs: Ascaris roundworms are acquired by swallowing eggs from contaminated soil or food. Heavy infections can impair nutrition or obstruct the bowel.
The worms inhabit the intestinal environment and interact with host immune responses. Their life cycle also includes migration through tissues before intestinal maturation.
Diagnosis and deworming address established infection. Sanitation and preventing soil contamination interrupt transmission; severe abdominal symptoms need assessment.
ascariasis.author: Gut Atlas seed

hookworm.title: Hookworm infection
hookworm.lead: Hookworm larvae usually enter through contaminated soil and develop into worms attached to the intestine.
paragraphs: Hookworm larvae usually enter through contaminated soil and develop into worms attached to the intestine. Chronic blood loss can cause iron-deficiency anaemia.
The worms feed at the lining and alter local immune activity. Iron status, nutrition and intestinal infection are directly connected in the disease process.
Anthelmintic treatment and correction of iron deficiency address different parts of recovery. Footwear and sanitation reduce exposure in endemic settings.
hookworm.author: Gut Atlas seed

trichuriasis.title: Whipworm infection
trichuriasis.lead: Trichuris whipworms infect the large intestine after eggs are swallowed.
paragraphs: Trichuris whipworms infect the large intestine after eggs are swallowed. Heavy burdens can cause abdominal pain, diarrhoea, anaemia and impaired growth.
Attachment in the bowel lining creates a sustained host–parasite interaction. Worm burden and nutrition matter alongside any accompanying bacterial-community changes.
Deworming and nutritional recovery are central. Safe sanitation and reducing soil contamination prevent repeated exposure.
trichuriasis.author: Gut Atlas seed

strongyloidiasis.title: Strongyloidiasis
strongyloidiasis.lead: Strongyloides can maintain infection through an internal reinfection cycle for years.
paragraphs: Strongyloides can maintain infection through an internal reinfection cycle for years. It may produce abdominal or skin symptoms and becomes dangerous during immunosuppression.
Its life cycle crosses the intestine and other tissues. Autoinfection distinguishes it from many other intestinal worms and explains persistent infection.
Exposure history and appropriate testing matter before immunosuppression in at-risk people. Ivermectin-based treatment is prescribed for confirmed or clinically relevant infection.
strongyloidiasis.author: Gut Atlas seed

pinworm.title: Pinworm infection
pinworm.lead: Pinworms commonly affect children and households, causing night-time itching around the anus.
paragraphs: Pinworms commonly affect children and households, causing night-time itching around the anus. Eggs spread through hands and contaminated surfaces.
The parasite’s reproductive cycle involves the large intestine and perianal skin. Symptoms arise from that cycle rather than a general loss of bacterial diversity.
Treatment often addresses household transmission as well as the infected person. Handwashing, short nails and washing bedding help reduce reinfection.
pinworm.author: Gut Atlas seed

hepatitis-a.title: Hepatitis A
hepatitis-a.lead: Hepatitis A is a liver infection spread through contaminated food, water or close contact.
paragraphs: Hepatitis A is a liver infection spread through contaminated food, water or close contact. It can cause fatigue, nausea and jaundice.
The transmission route is enteric, while the main tissue injury is in the liver. This separates the route of exposure from the organ affected.
Supportive care and monitoring address illness. Vaccination and post-exposure measures prevent infection in relevant settings; severe vomiting or worsening jaundice needs assessment.
hepatitis-a.author: Gut Atlas seed

hepatitis-b.title: Hepatitis B
hepatitis-b.lead: Hepatitis B spreads through infected blood and body fluids and can become chronic.
paragraphs: Hepatitis B spreads through infected blood and body fluids and can become chronic. Persistent infection increases the risk of cirrhosis and liver cancer.
The gut–liver circulation becomes relevant as liver disease changes bile handling and intestinal physiology. The causative agent itself is a hepatitis virus, not a gut bacterium.
Blood tests establish infection and assess activity. Vaccination prevents infection; monitoring and antiviral therapy address chronic disease when indicated.
hepatitis-b.author: Gut Atlas seed

hepatitis-c.title: Hepatitis C
hepatitis-c.lead: Hepatitis C is a blood-borne viral infection that often becomes chronic and can scar the liver.
paragraphs: Hepatitis C is a blood-borne viral infection that often becomes chronic and can scar the liver. Symptoms can be absent for many years.
Liver injury changes the host environment of the gut–liver axis. Researchers follow intestinal permeability and metabolites alongside viral clearance and liver recovery.
Screening and confirmatory RNA testing identify infection. Direct-acting antiviral medicines cure most treated infections, with follow-up tailored to liver damage and other risks.
hepatitis-c.author: Gut Atlas seed

cholera.title: Cholera
cholera.lead: Cholera is an intestinal infection that can cause rapid, profuse watery diarrhoea.
paragraphs: Cholera is an intestinal infection that can cause rapid, profuse watery diarrhoea. Severe fluid loss can become life-threatening within hours.
Toxigenic Vibrio cholerae alters intestinal fluid secretion. The disease illustrates a specific microbial mechanism producing a large physiological effect.
Prompt oral or intravenous rehydration saves lives. Antibiotics are used in selected cases; safe water, sanitation and vaccination help prevent outbreaks.
cholera.author: Gut Atlas seed

typhoid.title: Typhoid fever
typhoid.lead: Typhoid is a systemic infection caused by Salmonella Typhi, usually acquired through contaminated food or water.
paragraphs: Typhoid is a systemic infection caused by Salmonella Typhi, usually acquired through contaminated food or water. Prolonged fever and abdominal symptoms are common.
The organism enters through the intestine and can spread through the body. Persistent carriage and antimicrobial resistance are important parts of its ecology.
Diagnosis and effective antibiotics are essential. The regimen depends on local resistance and travel history; vaccination and safe water reduce risk.
typhoid.author: Gut Atlas seed

oral-thrush.title: Oral thrush
oral-thrush.lead: Oral thrush is overgrowth of Candida in the mouth, producing white patches or soreness.
paragraphs: Oral thrush is overgrowth of Candida in the mouth, producing white patches or soreness. Antibiotics, dentures and immune or metabolic conditions can contribute.
A normally resident yeast expands in a changed local environment. The mouth is its own habitat; oral overgrowth does not establish that there is invasive intestinal candidiasis.
Care addresses the local infection and contributing factors, with antifungal treatment when needed. Recurrent episodes can prompt assessment of medicines or underlying conditions.
oral-thrush.author: Gut Atlas seed

vaginal-candidiasis.title: Vulvovaginal candidiasis
vaginal-candidiasis.lead: Vulvovaginal candidiasis causes itching, irritation and discharge when Candida produces symptomatic infection.
paragraphs: Vulvovaginal candidiasis causes itching, irritation and discharge when Candida produces symptomatic infection. It can recur, and other conditions can cause similar symptoms.
The vaginal ecosystem has different chemistry and community structure from the gut. Research examines fungal growth, local immunity and exchanges between neighbouring body sites.
Diagnosis helps distinguish yeast infection from other causes. Antifungal treatment and, for recurrent disease, a tailored assessment guide care.
vaginal-candidiasis.author: Gut Atlas seed

bacterial-vaginosis.title: Bacterial vaginosis
bacterial-vaginosis.lead: Bacterial vaginosis involves a shift in the vaginal microbial community and can cause a characteristic discharge or odour.
paragraphs: Bacterial vaginosis involves a shift in the vaginal microbial community and can cause a characteristic discharge or odour. Recurrence is common.

This is a site-specific community change, often involving reduced lactobacillus dominance and expansion of anaerobes. It offers a clear example of habitat chemistry and community structure interacting.
Clinical assessment or testing establishes the diagnosis. Antibiotic treatment and management of recurrence follow clinical guidance.
bacterial-vaginosis.author: Gut Atlas seed

uti.title: Urinary tract infection
uti.lead: UTIs occur when microbes establish infection in the urinary tract.
paragraphs: UTIs occur when microbes establish infection in the urinary tract. Burning, urgency and frequency are common in bladder infection; fever or flank pain can signal kidney involvement.
Gut-associated bacteria, especially particular E. coli strains, can serve as a reservoir for urinary infection. The route between habitats is central to recurrence research.
Symptoms, urine testing and sometimes culture guide treatment. Fever, flank pain, pregnancy or systemic illness change the urgency and choice of care.
uti.author: Gut Atlas seed

kidney-stones.title: Kidney stones
kidney-stones.lead: Kidney stones form when substances crystallise in urine.
paragraphs: Kidney stones form when substances crystallise in urine. They can cause severe flank pain, blood in urine or obstruction.
Some intestinal organisms metabolise oxalate, and bowel disease or altered absorption can increase urinary stone risk. This is one route linking intestinal chemistry to another organ.
Treatment depends on stone size, location and infection. Prevention uses stone analysis, urine measurements, fluid intake and targeted dietary or medical changes.
kidney-stones.author: Gut Atlas seed

ckd.title: Chronic kidney disease
ckd.lead: CKD is a persistent reduction in kidney function or evidence of kidney damage.
paragraphs: CKD is a persistent reduction in kidney function or evidence of kidney damage. Diabetes and high blood pressure are common causes.
Microbial products normally cleared by the kidneys can accumulate as function declines. Urea reaching the intestine also changes the microbial environment, creating a two-way gut–kidney interaction.
Blood and urine tests track kidney function and albumin loss. Treatment addresses the cause, blood pressure, metabolic risks and complications, with individual dietary advice.
ckd.author: Gut Atlas seed

type-2-diabetes.title: Type 2 diabetes
type-2-diabetes.lead: Type 2 diabetes combines insulin resistance with inadequate insulin production, leading to high blood glucose.
paragraphs: Type 2 diabetes combines insulin resistance with inadequate insulin production, leading to high blood glucose. It affects blood vessels, nerves and other organs over time.

Studies investigate microbial metabolites, bile acids and immune signalling in glucose regulation. Medicines such as metformin also change gut communities, so treatment and disease effects need to be examined together.
Glucose monitoring, nutrition, movement and medicines support control. Care also addresses cardiovascular and kidney risks rather than glucose alone.
type-2-diabetes.author: Gut Atlas seed

type-1-diabetes.title: Type 1 diabetes
type-1-diabetes.lead: Type 1 diabetes results from immune destruction of insulin-producing cells.
paragraphs: Type 1 diabetes results from immune destruction of insulin-producing cells. Insulin replacement is essential, and onset can include thirst, frequent urination and weight loss.

Longitudinal studies investigate the intestinal community and immune development before diagnosis. Microbial changes are studied as part of disease development, distinct from the need for insulin treatment.
Insulin, glucose monitoring, education and nutrition are central. Vomiting, dehydration or rapid breathing with high glucose can indicate an emergency.
type-1-diabetes.author: Gut Atlas seed

obesity.title: Obesity
obesity.lead: Obesity involves excess adiposity that can affect metabolic, mechanical and psychological health.
paragraphs: Obesity involves excess adiposity that can affect metabolic, mechanical and psychological health. Genetics, food environments, sleep, medicines and physiology all contribute.

Microbes participate in energy extraction, metabolite production and host signalling. Studies of microbial interventions sit alongside research on diet, appetite regulation and the host’s metabolic state.
Care is individualised and can include nutritional support, activity, behavioural approaches, medicines or surgery. Health outcomes and sustained function matter alongside body weight.
obesity.author: Gut Atlas seed

metabolic-syndrome.title: Metabolic syndrome
metabolic-syndrome.lead: Metabolic syndrome groups abdominal adiposity, raised blood pressure, abnormal blood lipids and impaired glucose regulation.
paragraphs: Metabolic syndrome groups abdominal adiposity, raised blood pressure, abnormal blood lipids and impaired glucose regulation. Together these increase cardiovascular and diabetes risk.
Dietary substrates, microbial metabolites and liver–gut signalling are investigated across these connected features.
Care addresses blood pressure, glucose, lipids, food patterns and activity together. Treatment can include medicines targeted to the individual risks.
metabolic-syndrome.author: Gut Atlas seed

hypertension.title: High blood pressure
hypertension.lead: Hypertension is persistently raised blood pressure, often without symptoms.
paragraphs: Hypertension is persistently raised blood pressure, often without symptoms. Over time it damages the heart, brain, blood vessels and kidneys.
Research follows short-chain fatty acids, immune signalling and kidney–gut interactions. Dietary patterns can change both microbial substrates and blood pressure through several routes.
Repeated measurements establish the pattern. Activity, dietary changes and appropriate medicines reduce risk; management is based on measured pressure and overall health.
hypertension.author: Gut Atlas seed

coronary-heart-disease.title: Coronary heart disease
coronary-heart-disease.lead: Coronary disease develops when atherosclerosis limits blood flow to the heart.
paragraphs: Coronary disease develops when atherosclerosis limits blood flow to the heart. It can cause angina or an acute heart attack.

Microbial metabolism of dietary compounds, including the trimethylamine pathway, is investigated in vascular disease. These studies connect food, liver processing, kidney clearance and cardiovascular risk.
Care addresses lipids, blood pressure, smoking and other risks, with medicines and procedures when needed. New chest pressure or symptoms suggesting a heart attack require emergency care.
coronary-heart-disease.author: Gut Atlas seed

heart-failure.title: Heart failure
heart-failure.lead: Heart failure means the heart cannot fill or pump adequately for the body’s needs.
paragraphs: Heart failure means the heart cannot fill or pump adequately for the body’s needs. Breathlessness, fatigue and swelling are common.
Reduced blood flow and congestion can change intestinal function. Microbial metabolites and barrier changes are studied along this gut–heart route.
Assessment identifies the heart problem and contributing conditions. Medicines, monitoring and sometimes devices or procedures improve symptoms and outcomes.
heart-failure.author: Gut Atlas seed

stroke.title: Stroke
stroke.lead: A stroke occurs when brain blood flow is blocked or a blood vessel ruptures.
paragraphs: A stroke occurs when brain blood flow is blocked or a blood vessel ruptures. Sudden weakness, speech problems or visual changes are warning signs.
The gut–brain axis is investigated during inflammation and recovery after stroke. Feeding, mobility and medications also reshape the intestinal environment during rehabilitation.
Suspected stroke is an emergency. Rapid assessment determines treatment, followed by prevention of another event and rehabilitation.
stroke.author: Gut Atlas seed

high-cholesterol.title: High cholesterol
high-cholesterol.lead: Abnormal blood lipid levels can increase atherosclerotic cardiovascular risk.
paragraphs: Abnormal blood lipid levels can increase atherosclerotic cardiovascular risk. Many people have no symptoms and learn about them through blood testing.
Bile-acid recycling and microbial transformations connect intestinal metabolism with lipid handling. Dietary fibre also acts through processes that include bile-acid binding and fermentation.
Care uses lipid measurements and overall cardiovascular risk to guide food changes and medicines. Inherited lipid disorders may need especially intensive treatment.
high-cholesterol.author: Gut Atlas seed

gout.title: Gout
gout.lead: Gout is inflammatory arthritis caused by urate crystals, often producing sudden severe pain in a joint.
paragraphs: Gout is inflammatory arthritis caused by urate crystals, often producing sudden severe pain in a joint. Kidney handling of urate, genetics and metabolic factors contribute.
Intestinal urate transport and microbial purine metabolism are studied as additional parts of urate balance. These routes complement the established kidney and joint biology.
Acute attacks and long-term urate control require different treatment strategies. A clinician can guide anti-inflammatory treatment, urate-lowering therapy and relevant dietary changes.
gout.author: Gut Atlas seed

rheumatoid-arthritis.title: Rheumatoid arthritis
rheumatoid-arthritis.lead: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disease causing persistent joint inflammation, stiffness and potential damage.
paragraphs: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disease causing persistent joint inflammation, stiffness and potential damage. It can affect organs beyond the joints.
Studies investigate mucosal immune responses and microbes in the mouth and intestine before and after disease onset. The questions include microbial antigens, barrier function and treatment effects.
Early assessment and disease-modifying treatment help prevent damage. Care also includes activity, symptom control and monitoring for systemic effects.
rheumatoid-arthritis.author: Gut Atlas seed

osteoarthritis.title: Osteoarthritis
osteoarthritis.lead: Osteoarthritis involves changes across the whole joint, including cartilage, bone and surrounding tissues.
paragraphs: Osteoarthritis involves changes across the whole joint, including cartilage, bone and surrounding tissues. Pain and reduced function often affect knees, hips or hands.
Researchers investigate metabolic inflammation and microbial products in joint symptoms. Mechanical loading, injury and local tissue changes remain essential parts of the condition.
Exercise, strength, weight management when relevant and pain treatment support function. Joint replacement is an option for some advanced disease.
osteoarthritis.author: Gut Atlas seed

psoriasis.title: Psoriasis
psoriasis.lead: Psoriasis is an immune-mediated condition producing inflamed, scaly skin.
paragraphs: Psoriasis is an immune-mediated condition producing inflamed, scaly skin. Some people also develop psoriatic arthritis.

Research examines immune pathways shared between skin and gut, including microbial metabolites and inflammatory signalling. Skin communities and gut communities are separate habitats in these studies.
Treatment ranges from topical therapies to phototherapy and systemic medicines. Joint pain or swelling warrants assessment for associated arthritis.
psoriasis.author: Gut Atlas seed

eczema.title: Atopic eczema
eczema.lead: Atopic eczema causes itchy, inflamed skin with an impaired barrier.
paragraphs: Atopic eczema causes itchy, inflamed skin with an impaired barrier. It often begins in childhood and can fluctuate with exposures and infection.
Early-life immune development and intestinal communities are studied alongside the skin barrier. Staphylococcus aureus on affected skin is a different, local microbial interaction.
Emollients, anti-inflammatory skin treatment and avoiding identified irritants support control. More severe disease can need specialist therapies.
eczema.author: Gut Atlas seed

acne.title: Acne
acne.lead: Acne develops in hair follicles through interactions among sebum, blocked pores, inflammation and Cutibacterium acnes.
paragraphs: Acne develops in hair follicles through interactions among sebum, blocked pores, inflammation and Cutibacterium acnes. It can cause persistent scars and psychological distress.
Its direct microbial habitat is the skin follicle. Gut research explores dietary and systemic inflammatory connections, which are distinct from the established local skin mechanism.
Topical retinoids, benzoyl peroxide and other treatments are selected by severity. Persistent or scarring acne benefits from clinical assessment.
acne.author: Gut Atlas seed

rosacea.title: Rosacea
rosacea.lead: Rosacea causes facial flushing, persistent redness and sometimes inflammatory bumps or eye symptoms.
paragraphs: Rosacea causes facial flushing, persistent redness and sometimes inflammatory bumps or eye symptoms. Individual triggers and disease patterns vary.

Researchers investigate skin immunity, Demodex-associated responses and links with gastrointestinal conditions. These are several different biological routes rather than a single organism explaining all rosacea.
Sun protection, trigger management and prescribed skin or eye treatments support control. Eye pain or vision changes require assessment.
rosacea.author: Gut Atlas seed

seborrhoeic-dermatitis.title: Seborrhoeic dermatitis
seborrhoeic-dermatitis.lead: Seborrhoeic dermatitis causes scaling and inflammation in oily skin areas such as the scalp, face and chest.
paragraphs: Seborrhoeic dermatitis causes scaling and inflammation in oily skin areas such as the scalp, face and chest. Dandruff is a milder presentation.
Malassezia yeasts interact with skin lipids and host inflammatory responses. This is a local fungal habitat, which should be distinguished from Malassezia findings in gut research.
Antifungal shampoos or creams and short courses of anti-inflammatory treatments can help. Persistent or unusual presentations deserve assessment.
seborrhoeic-dermatitis.author: Gut Atlas seed

asthma.title: Asthma
asthma.lead: Asthma involves variable airway narrowing and inflammation, producing wheeze, breathlessness or cough.
paragraphs: Asthma involves variable airway narrowing and inflammation, producing wheeze, breathlessness or cough. Triggers and inflammatory patterns differ between people.
Early-life gut communities and microbial metabolites are studied in the development of airway immunity. Respiratory and intestinal habitats are connected through host immune pathways.
Diagnosis uses the symptom pattern and breathing tests where appropriate. Inhaled treatment, trigger management and an action plan reduce attacks.
asthma.author: Gut Atlas seed

allergic-rhinitis.title: Allergic rhinitis
allergic-rhinitis.lead: Allergic rhinitis causes sneezing, itching, congestion and watery discharge after exposure to allergens such as pollen or dust mites..
paragraphs: Allergic rhinitis causes sneezing, itching, congestion and watery discharge after exposure to allergens such as pollen or dust mites.
Studies investigate how microbial exposure and immune development influence allergic responses. The nasal community and intestinal community are different parts of that environment.
Allergen management, nasal corticosteroids, antihistamines and sometimes immunotherapy help control symptoms. Persistent obstruction can have additional causes.
allergic-rhinitis.author: Gut Atlas seed

food-allergy.title: Food allergy
food-allergy.lead: Food allergy is an immune reaction to a food and can affect the skin, gut, breathing or circulation.
paragraphs: Food allergy is an immune reaction to a food and can affect the skin, gut, breathing or circulation. It differs from difficulty digesting a food such as lactose intolerance.
The intestinal barrier and development of immune tolerance are central research areas. Microbial metabolites are investigated for their effects on these processes.
Diagnosis uses history and appropriate testing, sometimes with supervised food challenges. Avoidance plans and emergency treatment are tailored to the confirmed allergy.
food-allergy.author: Gut Atlas seed

anaphylaxis.title: Anaphylaxis
anaphylaxis.lead: Anaphylaxis is a rapidly developing, potentially life-threatening allergic reaction involving breathing, circulation or several body systems..
paragraphs: Anaphylaxis is a rapidly developing, potentially life-threatening allergic reaction involving breathing, circulation or several body systems.
Food can trigger anaphylaxis through immune pathways involving the gut, but the immediate event is a systemic emergency. Microbiome research on allergy prevention addresses a different timescale.
Use prescribed adrenaline promptly and call emergency services for suspected anaphylaxis. Follow-up identifies the trigger and establishes an emergency plan.
anaphylaxis.author: Gut Atlas seed

chronic-urticaria.title: Chronic urticaria
chronic-urticaria.lead: Chronic urticaria causes recurrent itchy wheals, sometimes with deeper swelling, for more than six weeks.
paragraphs: Chronic urticaria causes recurrent itchy wheals, sometimes with deeper swelling, for more than six weeks. Many cases involve spontaneous immune activation rather than a specific food allergy.
Studies examine immune signalling, infections and intestinal communities in some patient groups. The clinical pattern and response to treatment are more informative than broad food-exclusion lists.
Antihistamines are commonly used, with specialist treatments for persistent disease. Breathing or circulatory symptoms with swelling need urgent care.
chronic-urticaria.author: Gut Atlas seed

lupus.title: Systemic lupus erythematosus
lupus.lead: Lupus is an autoimmune disease that can affect skin, joints, kidneys, blood and other organs.
paragraphs: Lupus is an autoimmune disease that can affect skin, joints, kidneys, blood and other organs. Its manifestations and activity vary substantially.
Research investigates microbial antigens and immune cross-reactivity at mucosal surfaces. These studies examine mechanisms that may differ between lupus subgroups.
Care follows the organs affected and can include antimalarial and immune-modifying medicines. Monitoring detects flares and treatment complications.
lupus.author: Gut Atlas seed

multiple-sclerosis.title: Multiple sclerosis
multiple-sclerosis.lead: Multiple sclerosis is an immune-mediated disease affecting the brain and spinal cord, producing varied neurological symptoms..
paragraphs: Multiple sclerosis is an immune-mediated disease affecting the brain and spinal cord, producing varied neurological symptoms.
Human cohorts and experimental systems investigate intestinal microbes, metabolites and immune-cell activity. Disease-modifying medicines and disability can also alter the gut environment.
Neurological assessment and imaging guide diagnosis. Disease-modifying treatment, rehabilitation and symptom management address different parts of care.
multiple-sclerosis.author: Gut Atlas seed

depression.title: Depression
depression.lead: Depression affects mood, interest, thinking, sleep and daily function.
paragraphs: Depression affects mood, interest, thinking, sleep and daily function. Physical symptoms and changes in appetite can accompany it.
Studies investigate gut microbial functions, immune signals and tryptophan metabolism in relation to mood. Human cohort findings and intervention studies answer different questions.
Psychological therapies, medicines and practical support are effective components of care. Severe impairment or thoughts of self-harm require prompt professional support.
depression.author: Gut Atlas seed

anxiety.title: Generalised anxiety disorder
anxiety.lead: Generalised anxiety disorder involves persistent, difficult-to-control worry with physical tension, sleep disturbance or other symptoms affecting daily life..
paragraphs: Generalised anxiety disorder involves persistent, difficult-to-control worry with physical tension, sleep disturbance or other symptoms affecting daily life.
The gut–brain relationship includes autonomic activity, immune signals and microbial metabolism. Stress can also change digestion, so direction of effect is part of the research.
Psychological therapy, appropriate medicines and support for sleep and daily function can help. Assessment also considers physical conditions or medicines that mimic anxiety.
anxiety.author: Gut Atlas seed

bipolar.title: Bipolar disorder
bipolar.lead: Bipolar disorder involves episodes of depression and mania or hypomania, with changes in mood, energy, sleep and behaviour..
paragraphs: Bipolar disorder involves episodes of depression and mania or hypomania, with changes in mood, energy, sleep and behaviour.
Microbial metabolism and inflammation are studied alongside established brain and circadian biology. Medicines, food intake and sleep changes are important influences on gut measurements.
Specialist assessment and mood-stabilising treatment are central. Recognising changes in sleep and early episode signs supports an individual care plan.
bipolar.author: Gut Atlas seed

schizophrenia.title: Schizophrenia
schizophrenia.lead: Schizophrenia can involve hallucinations, delusions, disorganised thinking and changes in motivation or cognition.
paragraphs: Schizophrenia can involve hallucinations, delusions, disorganised thinking and changes in motivation or cognition. It requires sustained clinical and social support.

Research examines immune signals, microbial metabolites and the effects of antipsychotic medicines on metabolic and intestinal health. These are complementary biological questions, not a replacement for psychiatric care.
Treatment combines appropriate medicines, psychological and social support and attention to physical health. New psychotic symptoms need prompt assessment.
schizophrenia.author: Gut Atlas seed

parkinsons.title: Parkinson’s disease
parkinsons.lead: Parkinson’s disease affects movement and can also cause constipation, sleep changes and other non-motor symptoms..
paragraphs: Parkinson’s disease affects movement and can also cause constipation, sleep changes and other non-motor symptoms.

The enteric nervous system, intestinal inflammation and microbial metabolism are studied in disease biology. Microbes can also metabolise some medicines, making treatment exposure an additional research question.
Neurological treatment, movement, rehabilitation and management of non-motor symptoms support function. Constipation and nutrition deserve attention alongside motor care.
parkinsons.author: Gut Atlas seed

alzheimers.title: Alzheimer’s disease
alzheimers.lead: Alzheimer’s disease causes progressive difficulties with memory and other cognitive functions.
paragraphs: Alzheimer’s disease causes progressive difficulties with memory and other cognitive functions. Daily activities and independence become increasingly affected.
Studies examine microbial products, vascular health and immune signalling along the gut–brain axis. Food intake, ageing and medicines are also relevant to the gut environment in affected people.
Assessment distinguishes causes of cognitive decline. Care combines appropriate treatments, support for daily life and safety, and help for caregivers.
alzheimers.author: Gut Atlas seed

migraine.title: Migraine
migraine.lead: Migraine causes recurrent attacks of head pain with symptoms such as nausea, light sensitivity or aura.
paragraphs: Migraine causes recurrent attacks of head pain with symptoms such as nausea, light sensitivity or aura. It is a neurological disorder with varied triggers.
Gut motility, nausea, shared signalling molecules and intestinal disorders are examined in migraine research. The connection also affects how oral medicines are absorbed during attacks.
Acute and preventive treatments are selected according to attack frequency and disability. A new or abrupt severe headache needs assessment for other causes.
migraine.author: Gut Atlas seed

epilepsy.title: Epilepsy
epilepsy.lead: Epilepsy involves a persistent tendency to recurrent seizures.
paragraphs: Epilepsy involves a persistent tendency to recurrent seizures. Seizure types and underlying causes vary.
Dietary therapies for some drug-resistant epilepsies change metabolism and microbial substrates. Experimental work investigates which microbial functions participate in these treatment effects.
Diagnosis and antiseizure treatment are tailored to seizure type and cause. Specialised dietary treatment requires supervised nutritional and neurological care.
epilepsy.author: Gut Atlas seed

autism.title: Autism spectrum condition
autism.lead: Autism is a neurodevelopmental condition affecting communication, sensory processing and patterns of behaviour or interests.
paragraphs: Autism is a neurodevelopmental condition affecting communication, sensory processing and patterns of behaviour or interests. Support needs vary widely.
Gut research often concerns co-occurring constipation, pain or feeding difficulties. Food selectivity, medicines and gastrointestinal symptoms are important when interpreting community measurements.
Support is individualised and includes communication, sensory and educational needs. Gastrointestinal symptoms deserve direct assessment.
autism.author: Gut Atlas seed

adhd.title: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder
adhd.lead: ADHD affects attention, impulse regulation or activity levels in ways that impair daily function.
paragraphs: ADHD affects attention, impulse regulation or activity levels in ways that impair daily function. It can continue into adulthood.
Researchers study diet, microbial metabolites and gut–brain signalling alongside neurodevelopmental and genetic factors. Sleep and appetite changes can also affect the gut indirectly.
Assessment considers settings, functional difficulties and other conditions. Behavioural support, environmental adjustments and medicines can be helpful.
adhd.author: Gut Atlas seed

insomnia.title: Insomnia
insomnia.lead: Insomnia involves persistent difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep or waking too early with daytime consequences..
paragraphs: Insomnia involves persistent difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep or waking too early with daytime consequences.

Sleep–wake timing and meals affect the intestinal environment. Human sleep-restriction studies measure changes in microbial richness and circulating metabolites rather than diagnosing insomnia from stool.
Cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia addresses persistent problems. Assessment also considers medicines, sleep apnoea and other contributing conditions.
insomnia.author: Gut Atlas seed

sleep-apnoea.title: Obstructive sleep apnoea
sleep-apnoea.lead: Obstructive sleep apnoea causes repeated upper-airway collapse during sleep, with disrupted breathing and sleep quality..
paragraphs: Obstructive sleep apnoea causes repeated upper-airway collapse during sleep, with disrupted breathing and sleep quality.
Intermittent low oxygen and metabolic changes are studied in relation to gut inflammation and microbial products. Obesity, diet and treatment are important accompanying factors.
Sleep testing establishes the diagnosis. Airway treatments, positive-pressure therapy and other interventions are chosen according to severity and anatomy.
sleep-apnoea.author: Gut Atlas seed

iron-deficiency.title: Iron-deficiency anaemia
iron-deficiency.lead: Iron deficiency reduces the body’s capacity to make haemoglobin, causing fatigue, reduced exercise tolerance or other symptoms.
paragraphs: Iron deficiency reduces the body’s capacity to make haemoglobin, causing fatigue, reduced exercise tolerance or other symptoms. Blood loss and inadequate absorption or intake are common routes.
The gut absorbs iron and is a site where blood loss or disease can create deficiency. Iron supplements also change the resources available to intestinal microbes.
Care identifies the cause as well as replacing iron. Heavy menstrual bleeding, gastrointestinal bleeding and coeliac disease are among the possible contributors.
iron-deficiency.author: Gut Atlas seed

b12-deficiency.title: Vitamin B12 deficiency
b12-deficiency.lead: B12 deficiency can cause anaemia, numbness, balance problems or cognitive symptoms.
paragraphs: B12 deficiency can cause anaemia, numbness, balance problems or cognitive symptoms. Neurological effects can occur without obvious anaemia.
Absorption depends on stomach and small-intestinal processes, including intrinsic factor. Gastric autoimmunity, surgery, ileal disease and some medicines can interfere with this pathway.
Testing and the clinical picture guide oral or injected replacement. New neurological symptoms need timely assessment and treatment.
b12-deficiency.author: Gut Atlas seed

hypothyroidism.title: Hypothyroidism
hypothyroidism.lead: Hypothyroidism is insufficient thyroid hormone production, which can cause fatigue, cold intolerance, constipation and other changes..
paragraphs: Hypothyroidism is insufficient thyroid hormone production, which can cause fatigue, cold intolerance, constipation and other changes.
Thyroid hormones influence intestinal motility. Research also examines autoimmune and microbial relationships, while constipation itself changes transit and fermentation.
Blood tests establish thyroid function. Hormone replacement and monitoring guide treatment; timing with food, iron and other medicines can affect absorption.
hypothyroidism.author: Gut Atlas seed

hyperthyroidism.title: Hyperthyroidism
hyperthyroidism.lead: Excess thyroid hormone can cause palpitations, heat intolerance, weight loss and frequent bowel movements.
paragraphs: Excess thyroid hormone can cause palpitations, heat intolerance, weight loss and frequent bowel movements. Graves’ disease is a common cause.
Hormone-driven changes in transit and metabolism alter the digestive environment. Microbial findings need to be interpreted alongside these strong physiological effects.
Blood tests and investigation of the cause guide antithyroid medicines, radioiodine or surgery. Significant heart or systemic symptoms need prompt assessment.
hyperthyroidism.author: Gut Atlas seed

pcos.title: Polycystic ovary syndrome
pcos.lead: PCOS involves combinations of ovulatory dysfunction, androgen excess and characteristic ovarian findings.
paragraphs: PCOS involves combinations of ovulatory dysfunction, androgen excess and characteristic ovarian findings. Insulin resistance and metabolic risks are common.

Studies examine microbial metabolites and metabolic inflammation alongside hormonal and reproductive features. Food patterns, body composition and medicines are important influences on the measurements.
Care follows the person’s priorities, including cycles, symptoms, fertility and metabolic health. Nutrition, activity and appropriate medicines are selected accordingly.
pcos.author: Gut Atlas seed

endometriosis.title: Endometriosis
endometriosis.lead: Endometriosis involves tissue similar to the uterine lining growing outside the uterus.
paragraphs: Endometriosis involves tissue similar to the uterine lining growing outside the uterus. Pelvic pain, painful periods and fertility difficulties can result.
Intestinal symptoms can overlap with pelvic disease. Research investigates immune activity, hormone metabolism and microbial communities at several body sites.
Assessment and treatment can include pain management, hormonal therapy or surgery according to symptoms and fertility goals. Bowel symptoms also warrant their own evaluation.
endometriosis.author: Gut Atlas seed

periodontitis.title: Periodontitis
periodontitis.lead: Periodontitis is inflammatory destruction of tissues supporting the teeth.
paragraphs: Periodontitis is inflammatory destruction of tissues supporting the teeth. It can lead to gum recession, loose teeth and tooth loss.
Dental biofilms and host inflammation directly drive the local disease process. Oral organisms and inflammatory signals are also studied in relation to systemic and gut conditions.
Professional periodontal treatment and sustained daily plaque control are central. Smoking, diabetes and other contributing factors affect disease and healing.
periodontitis.author: Gut Atlas seed

dental-caries.title: Dental caries
dental-caries.lead: Dental caries develops when repeated acid production in dental plaque causes mineral loss from teeth.
paragraphs: Dental caries develops when repeated acid production in dental plaque causes mineral loss from teeth. Sugar exposure, saliva and fluoride influence the balance.
This is a clear community-and-chemistry mechanism: oral microbes ferment carbohydrates, lowering local pH. Frequent exposures can sustain conditions favouring acid-tolerant organisms.
Fluoride, effective cleaning, sugar-exposure patterns and dental treatment address different stages. Pain, swelling or a dental abscess need prompt care.
dental-caries.author: Gut Atlas seed

gingivitis.title: Gingivitis
gingivitis.lead: Gingivitis is inflammation of the gums, often causing bleeding with cleaning.
paragraphs: Gingivitis is inflammation of the gums, often causing bleeding with cleaning. It can improve when dental plaque and contributing factors are addressed.
A biofilm accumulates at the gum margin and stimulates a local immune response. The same organisms can behave differently in a changed community and habitat.
Daily plaque control and professional cleaning support recovery. Persistent bleeding should be checked for periodontal disease and other contributors.
gingivitis.author: Gut Atlas seed

common-cold.title: Common cold
common-cold.lead: The common cold is a viral upper-respiratory infection causing a runny nose, sore throat and cough.
paragraphs: The common cold is a viral upper-respiratory infection causing a runny nose, sore throat and cough. Several different viruses can produce the syndrome.
The primary infected habitat is respiratory. Gut research examines immune development and host responses to infections, rather than treating the cold as an intestinal infection.
Rest, fluids and symptom relief are usually sufficient. Antibiotics do not treat cold viruses; difficulty breathing or persistent worsening symptoms warrant assessment.
common-cold.author: Gut Atlas seed

influenza.title: Influenza
influenza.lead: Influenza is a respiratory viral infection that can cause fever, muscle aches, cough and marked fatigue.
paragraphs: Influenza is a respiratory viral infection that can cause fever, muscle aches, cough and marked fatigue. Some people develop serious complications.

Experimental work investigates how intestinal microbes and their products influence antiviral immunity. The virus primarily infects the respiratory tract, distinguishing the immune link from the infected site.
Vaccination reduces risk. Antiviral treatment is particularly important for severe illness or higher-risk people and is most useful when started promptly.
influenza.author: Gut Atlas seed

covid.title: COVID-19
covid.lead: COVID-19 can affect the respiratory tract and other systems and sometimes causes gastrointestinal symptoms.
paragraphs: COVID-19 can affect the respiratory tract and other systems and sometimes causes gastrointestinal symptoms. Severity and recovery vary.
SARS-CoV-2 can involve intestinal cells. Research follows gut-community changes, immune activity and persistent symptoms, alongside effects of medicines and illness severity.
Testing, risk assessment and current treatment guidance inform care. Breathing difficulty or other severe symptoms need urgent assessment; persistent symptoms deserve follow-up.
covid.author: Gut Atlas seed

pneumonia.title: Pneumonia
pneumonia.lead: Pneumonia is infection of lung tissue caused by bacteria, viruses or other organisms.
paragraphs: Pneumonia is infection of lung tissue caused by bacteria, viruses or other organisms. It can cause cough, fever, breathlessness and chest pain.
The mouth and respiratory tract can provide organisms involved in infection. Research also examines gut-mediated immune responses and the intestinal effects of antibiotic treatment.
Assessment establishes severity and likely cause. Treatment can involve antibiotics, antivirals, oxygen or supportive care according to the infection and the person’s condition.
pneumonia.author: Gut Atlas seed

sinusitis.title: Sinusitis
sinusitis.lead: Sinusitis involves inflammation of the sinus lining, commonly following a viral infection or with ongoing inflammatory disease.
paragraphs: Sinusitis involves inflammation of the sinus lining, commonly following a viral infection or with ongoing inflammatory disease. Facial pressure and nasal symptoms are common.
The local microbial habitat is the nose and sinuses. Treatments such as antibiotics can also affect intestinal communities; these are different sites and mechanisms.
Care depends on duration, severity and cause. Most short viral episodes do not need antibiotics, while persistent or complicated disease warrants assessment.
sinusitis.author: Gut Atlas seed

breast-cancer.title: Breast cancer
breast-cancer.lead: Breast cancer includes several tumour types with different hormone receptors and molecular features.
paragraphs: Breast cancer includes several tumour types with different hormone receptors and molecular features. These distinctions guide treatment.
Research explores microbial hormone metabolism, immune signalling and interactions with cancer therapies. The gut route is a research context alongside established tumour biology and inherited risk.
Screening, imaging and biopsy establish the diagnosis. Surgery, radiotherapy and systemic treatments are selected according to stage and tumour characteristics.
breast-cancer.author: Gut Atlas seed
